cards.explanation: The answer is False. The text says Israel was defeated by the Philistines, who struck down about four thousand men on the battlefield (1 Samuel 4:2). It's a rough opening to the story. Hold on to that, friends, because Israel's next move comes right out of this loss.

The plan is to bring the ark from Shiloh. The elders say, “Let us bring the ark of the covenant of the LORD from Shiloh, so that it may go with us to save us from the hand of our enemies.” The ark is to come from Shiloh and go with them. So the plan is to haul it out to the battle.

The answer is True. The elders say the ark should come “…so that it may go with us to save us from the hand of our enemies.” That's what they're hoping for. I'll just say it plainly, friends: the plan is built around the ark going with them.

The two men are Hophni and Phinehas. The verse says the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were there with the ark of the covenant of God. Eli is the one who has been judging Israel. Remember these two names, bakers, because they come up again in this passage.

The answer is True. The verse says all the Israelites raised such a great shout that the ground shook. I've been in a crowd so loud I felt it in my feet, but I've never felt the ground itself shake. That's a LOT of shouting.

The word is afraid. When they realized the ark of the LORD had entered the camp, the Philistines were afraid. They cry out, “The gods have entered their camp!” They also say, “Woe to us, for nothing like this has happened before.”

The answer is Egyptians. The Philistines say, “These are the gods who struck the Egyptians with all kinds of plagues in the wilderness.” They've heard the old stories about Egypt, friends. They don't look relieved to be remembering them.

The Philistines tell each other to take courage and fight. They say, “Take courage and be men, O Philistines!” and then, “Now be men and fight!” They're afraid, and they tell each other to fight anyway.

Israel is defeated and thirty thousand fall. The Philistines fought, Israel was defeated, and each man fled to his tent. The slaughter was very great, and thirty thousand foot soldiers of Israel fell. It's a heavy verse, friends, and the second battle is far worse than the first.
The Philistines capture the ark. The verse says it plainly: “The ark of God was captured…” Israel brought it into battle to save them, and in the end the Philistines are the ones who take it.
The answer is False, and it's a hard verse. It says the ark of God was captured and Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died. They had been there with the ark. I think this one hurts, friends.

The word is ark. The verse says Eli sat on his chair beside the road, watching, because his heart trembled for the ark of God. That's a tender detail about him. I think he had a lot riding on that ark.

The answer is True. The verse says that when the man entered the city to give a report, the whole city cried out. Before he says a word to Eli, the whole city is crying out, friends. Eli hears the noise and asks about it.

The news is that Israel fled, his sons died and the ark was taken. The messenger says, “Israel has fled before the Philistines, and there has been a great slaughter among the people. Your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, are both dead, and the ark of God has been captured.” It's three heavy pieces in one report.

It's the ark of God. The verse says, “As soon as the ark of God was mentioned, Eli fell backward from his chair by the city gate…” He heard about his sons and the army first, and it's the ark that comes right before he falls. I think that fits Eli's heart trembling for the ark, friends.

The answer is forty. The verse closes Eli's story with, “And Eli had judged Israel forty years.” That's a long time to lead. Forty years of judging, bakers, and the verse sums it up in one short line.

She collapses and gives birth, and it's a heavy moment. She hears about the capture of God's ark and the deaths of her father-in-law and her husband. Then the verse says, “…she collapsed and gave birth, for her labor pains overtook her.”

The answer is False, and it's a sad verse. The women say, “Do not be afraid, for you have given birth to a son!” The text says, “But she did not respond or pay any heed.” I think the weight of that day is hard to hold.

She says, “The glory has departed from Israel…” She names the boy Ichabod because the ark of God had been captured and her father-in-law and her husband had been killed. It's a heavy name for a baby, friends. The name carries what she said that day.
